_comment: Accepted risks, read by .github/scripts/verdict.py accepted(): an entry
matches a finding by control + id (+ optional `match` substring), never
expires silently (the date is checked) and is recorded in the verdict
detail and the findings table so it stays visible.
Every entry here is about the TEST HARNESS, not about the app: the
environment stand-in ingress is a Caddy container with a locally generated
CA (tests/env/Caddyfile), because the test runner has to reach the pod from
outside the cluster over TLS. The production path uses the cluster ingress

accepted.reason: The harness CA publishes no OCSP or CRL endpoints, so revocation status cannot be evaluated at all. A public certificate served by a real ingress is checked by the browser and by the dashboard's own probe; nothing about this deployment is learned by failing it here.
Caddy's internal intermediate CA is short-lived and rotated by Caddy itself on restart. Its expiry is a property of the ephemeral harness CA, not of the service certificate under test.
Same internal intermediate CA: notAfter is regenerated with the CA on every harness start.
